issues: The "spotlight" on the cream page is just a warm blob; the whole page stays bright, so there is no light-versus-dark contrast
The pool has a fairly hard edge and blows the white card out in the centre, reading as a disc stuck on the page rather than stage light
After the push-in the annotation is cropped by the left edge and sits on top of the neighbouring card's text
The annotation exits before the card reseats, so the last frame is just an oblique close-up with no message
changes: Look switched to graphite: the real page screenshot is kept but the house lights go down to 6-14% brightness, with true colour only inside the pool; the lamp strikes on with an on-dip-steady flicker

The roaming pool has a near-Gaussian falloff with a gentle tungsten tint and a volumetric shaft from far above frame with dust in the beam; after the lock it hands over to a page-space card-shaped light: the darkened page gets a soft card-shaped hole, so the card is lit edge to edge at native text contrast with falloff only outside it, plus a warm rim around the card

The camera focus shifts left so the card sits right of centre and the left side is free for the annotation: two lines of bold white sans with a champagne highlighter that flips the words to ink, over a dark scrim, drawn with the same camera on a layer above the lighting
The annotation no longer exits early; it settles back onto the page plane together with the card. The card's shadow falls lower-left, matching the light, and a champagne ring flashes on touchdown

Perimeter beam recoloured to champagne gold with a white core for its two laps; duration 139 to 172f, 3.6s from lock to touchdown, and the final second holds a locked camera with only the light breathing
